quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
You must turn right in this lane.
You can only turn right when you see a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow-green warning signs alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns you of sharp curves and turns ahead.

questions.question: A railroad crossbuck sign works the same way as a yield sign.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A railroad crossing sign acts like a yield sign. You must let any trains or railroad equipment pass before you go.

questions.question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always let them cross, even if they are breaking the law.
Only let them cross if they have the right to do so.
Slow down and honk near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always let them cross, even if they are breaking the law.
questions.explanation: You must do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle, no matter what. Always watch for pedestrians and let them cross, even if they are jaywalking or crossing illegally.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They need more distance to stop than cars.
Air brakes help them stop quickly.
They turn easier than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They need more distance to stop than cars.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need twice as much distance to stop as cars at the same speed. A car going 55 mph stops in about 400 feet. A large truck at 55 mph needs about 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A side road is ahead.
Merge traffic.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a side road will meet the main road ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in that direction.
You can turn in that direction after you stop.
You can turn in that direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means you must stop and cannot turn in that direction. Wait for a green arrow or green light to proceed.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean you cannot pass or change lanes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, or to turn onto or off a highway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: To merge into highway traffic safely:

options.text: Watch only the cars behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the car ahead.
Speed up and force the other cars to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Before you change lanes or enter traffic, check behind and beside your vehicle to make sure no cars are in your way.

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in your blood is called:

options.text: Implied consent (IC).
Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).

questions.correctAnswerText: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the amount of alcohol in your blood. The higher your BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: Drinking coffee after drinking alcohol:

options.text: Lowers your blood alcohol level.
Cancels out the alcohol.
Does not change your blood alcohol level.
Raises your blood alcohol level.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not change your blood alcohol level.
questions.explanation: Coffee does not lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC). It may keep you awake, but it cannot make you sober or change your BAC.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to leave the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: When it is hard to see because of darkness or bad weather, stay farther behind other cars. This gives you more time to react to dangers you may not see ahead.

questions.question: If a red light is on and a police officer tells you to go through the intersection, you should:

options.text: Stop until the light turns green.
Go through the intersection.
Come to a complete stop before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always follow a police officer's directions. A police officer's instructions override traffic lights and signs.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Use your turn signal before you reach the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to prepare to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always signal about 100 feet before turning left. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than other cars.
Drive at the posted speed limit.
Slow down.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When heavy rain makes it hard to see, slow down. Turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you. If rain is so heavy you cannot see clearly, pull to the side of the road and stop until it clears.

questions.question: At dawn, dusk, or in rain or snow, a good way to show other drivers you are there is to turn on your:

options.text: Dashboard lights.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when it is hard for other drivers to see you. Use low beam headlights whenever weather requires you to use your windshield wipers.

questions.question: When you see a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check for traffic only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, come to a full stop and check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Mistakes by drivers
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Mistakes by drivers
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or make unexpected moves. Talk to other drivers on the road to prevent crashes.

questions.question: You can cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The car in front of you moves right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line in the center means traffic next to it may pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: The best way to know if you can pass another vehicle is to check if:

options.text: There is a flashing green light ahead.
The road ahead is straight.
The car ahead signals that it is okay to pass.
The lane markings are solid or broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane markings are solid or broken.
questions.explanation: Lane markings down the center of the road show whether passing is allowed. On a two-lane highway, you cannot pass if your lane has a solid line next to it. Never pass within 100 feet of an intersection.

questions.question: A red arrow on a traffic light means you:

options.text: Can turn in that direction after slowing down and checking.
Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Can turn in that direction after stopping completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: A bad suspension system can cause:

options.text: Problems controlling the vehicle.
Squealing brakes.
Loose steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Problems controlling the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Suspension helps you control your vehicle and keeps the ride smooth on different road surfaces. If your car bounces a lot after hitting a bump or is hard to steer, you may need new suspension parts.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane when:

options.text: The driver you passed signals for you to return.
You signal for three seconds.
You see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You see the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you have enough space between you and the passed vehicle. Look in your rearview mirror. When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle, you have enough room to return safely to your lane.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect back off these weather conditions and create glare that makes it harder to see the road ahead.

questions.question: When driving in an area where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing the street.
Run out in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run out in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and could run in front of your vehicle without looking.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.
